planted.why_it_is_real: The integration job runs on merge_request_event, the settings export says merge-request pipelines are enabled for forks, and STAGING_DEPLOY_TOKEN is not protected, so a contributor's branch runs their own .gitlab-ci.yml with that token in the environment. Masked only hides it in the log.

planted.why_it_is_real: Groovy substitutes the change title into the double-quoted string before the shell parses it, so a title containing a quote and a semicolon runs commands on the agent.

planted.class: credential scoped to more processes than need it
planted.why_it_is_real: The publish token is in the environment of every child process of the block, including a vendored third-party script that has nothing to do with publishing.

planted.class: pipeline imported from a pointer that can move
planted.why_it_is_real: The build job definition is pulled from the default branch of another project, and the settings export says the whole engineering group can push to it, so anyone in that group can change what this pipeline runs.

planted.class: privileged shared runner reachable from an untrusted pipeline
planted.why_it_is_real: The shared runner is privileged and mounts the host Docker socket, and it is the runner that serves the merge-request pipeline of P-33, so contributor code runs as host root.

planted.class: a declared limit that nothing enforces
planted.why_it_is_real: MaxUploadMB is declared and assigned from MAX_UPLOAD_MB and read by nothing; the upload route is registered without BodyLimit and its handler does io.ReadAll on the body, so the configured cap is a knob the operator can set that changes nothing.

planted.class: an enforcer that exists and is never installed
planted.why_it_is_real: Throttle reads the configured burst and is registered on no route, so RATE_LIMIT_BURST is documented, settable and inert.

planted.class: a gate one sibling handler enforces and another does not
planted.why_it_is_real: CertificatesList.post builds AuthorityPermission and refuses when it cannot, and CertificatesUpload.post reaches the same effect - a certificate bound to a caller-named authority - with no check at all. The gate is in the same file, eleven lines up.

planted.class: authorization checked on the object in the path, not on the objects in the body
planted.why_it_is_real: The resolver turns caller-supplied ids into live certificates with no ownership scope, and appending them flips notify and superseded on rows the caller does not own, silencing somebody else's lifecycle automation.

planted.class: a length from the wire decides the size of an allocation
planted.why_it_is_real: The only test on the declared length excludes Integer.MAX_VALUE, which stops the cast from wrapping and lets every value below it through; the array is committed before readFully can fail, so five bytes on the wire ask for two gigabytes. Settings.MAX_FRAME_BYTES exists and this path never consults it.

planted.class: parser recursion with no depth cap
planted.why_it_is_real: readValue dispatches to readMap and readList, which call readValue again, and no signature on the cycle carries a depth parameter, so nesting costs the peer one byte per stack frame.

planted.class: a control that runs and cannot fail
planted.why_it_is_real: The expected digest is computed and then never compared: the only rejection is an empty signature, so any non-empty string authenticates any body.

planted.class: a configuration name nothing defines, and the default is the secret
planted.why_it_is_real: No compose file, env template or manifest in the case sets PARTNER_SIGNING_KEY, so the literal fallback is the signing key in every deployment that forgot it.

planted.class: a configuration name nothing defines, and the default is the secret
planted.why_it_is_real: SESSION_SECRET appears in no compose file, env template or manifest here; the fallback string is the session secret and it is readable in the repository.

planted.class: a configuration name nothing defines, and its absence turns a check off
planted.why_it_is_real: Nothing in the case defines VERIFY_WEBHOOK_AUDIENCE, so the default of "false" is the operative value and the audience check never runs.

planted.class: a control that runs and cannot fail
planted.why_it_is_real: The guard returns False only when the record does not exist; for any existing record it returns True, so the caller header is never consulted.

planted.class: a control that runs and cannot fail

planted.why_it_is_real: Third copy of the same guard, third module. Patching one of the three leaves the other two.

planted.class: attacker-controlled data written into a line-oriented log
planted.why_it_is_real: reason is concatenated into the record; a value carrying a newline forges a second audit line that nobody wrote.

planted.class: attacker-controlled data written into a line-oriented log
planted.why_it_is_real: Deferred %s formatting is not neutralisation: the logger writes the raw value, so a newline in submitter forges a record exactly as in P-51.

planted.class: a dependency that resolves and nothing in the project asks for
planted.why_it_is_real: It is the one requirement a reader cannot account for: it is pulled in only by app/tokens.py for bearer minting the project already does with hmac in app/security.py, and no other manifest, template or document mentions it.

planted.class: repository configuration that runs on the machine that opens the project
planted.why_it_is_real: A repository-scoped MCP server launched with npx -y and an unpinned @latest tag, with a signing key passed into its environment: opening the project runs whatever that name resolves to that day.

decoys.why: The query is scoped to req.user.id in the statement itself.
The interpolated column comes from a closed map, never from the request.
decode() feeds a metric label; authorization is resolved from the server-side session.
escapeHtml is applied at the sink.
The only interpolated value is Number(year); nothing external reaches it.
Host allowlist checked after parsing, with redirects disabled.
extractall(filter="data") rejects traversal and absolute names.
mkdtemp plus mkstemp: atomic, exclusive, inside a directory this process created.
The -- terminator is present and the path must already resolve.
0600 inside a 0700 per-user directory.
rmtree runs on a directory this process created in this run.
Scoped to two actions on one bucket prefix with an aws:ResourceAccount condition.
Read is granted to a CloudFront origin access identity, not to the world, and the object is marketing content.
443 open on an internet-facing load balancer is the point; the finding moves to what sits behind it.
The commit message travels through env: and is referenced as a quoted shell variable.
The action is pinned by commit SHA with persist-credentials disabled.
The download is verified against a pinned sha256 and the build refuses to continue on mismatch.
A template file whose values are placeholders and a documented test-mode key prefix.
Explicit scope mapping sends @acme to the internal registry, so a public package cannot take the name.
Small, functionally complete package with no recent release: assess issues and maintainer, do not report age alone.
Documents travel as separate blocks carrying origin and trust, delimited from the question.
The account id comes from the authenticated session and refunds are refused outright.
Only keys from a closed schema are stored, with a ttl.
The operation must be one of a closed set and nothing is executed.
The value is a ${VAR} substitution placeholder, not a secret.
Every indexed chunk carries origin and trust metadata that retrieval filters on.
An explicit field allowlist with a test that fails when a new field appears.
Only an opaque identifier is logged, and a redacting formatter covers anything else.
Identifiers are replaced by reversible tokens before the prompt is built.
Tags load only for the categories the visitor accepted.
The purge covers every store in the inventory, not only the primary.
There is no pull-request trigger, and the settings export states that secrets are not made available to builds of fork pull requests.
The interpolation lands in an environment variable, and the step that uses it is single-quoted, so the shell expands it as data rather than as script text.
The second include pins a commit SHA, which cannot be repointed.
One build per machine, no privileged flag, no Docker socket, and access_level restricts it to protected refs, so no untrusted principal reaches it.
The settings export shows the context restricted to a security group and fork builds receiving no secrets, and the job is filtered to main.
MaxBodyMB is read by BodyLimit, which is registered on the routes that carry a body; the reader exists and sits in the request chain.
It is consumed by NAME through the struct tag rather than by symbol, so a symbol search finds no reader while the enforcement is real.
CertificatesStats.get has no gate while its sibling post does, but the two do not reach the same effect: get returns aggregate counts by month and carries nothing of any caller.
The tags field names other rows in the body, but the resolver iterates the caller's own tags and keeps only the intersection, so an id the caller does not own resolves to nothing.
Identical shape to readBlob, but the declared length is compared against Settings.MAX_STRING_BYTES - a bound the peer does not set - on the line before the allocation.

It allocates from a declared length with no explicit check, which is the shape, but readUnsignedShort bounds the value to 65535 by its own type, so the largest allocation the peer can ask for is 64 KiB.
Same shape as P-44 and one line apart in the reading, but it ends in hmac.compare_digest over both operands.
The fourth guard in the family is the one that works: it compares the record owner against the caller.
Read with a fallback like P-46, but docker-compose.yml and .env.example both define it, which a reader checks in one step.
Defined in both deployment files, and the default decides a page size rather than a security property.
The value reaches the log through json.dumps, which escapes the control characters that would forge a record.
An unusual-looking name and version next to P-53, and an ordinary, long-established, widely installed package.
Repository-scoped editor configuration that names no program and overrides no setting of the reader: it is data.
An instruction file that steers a generator, carrying house style only: no invisible characters and nothing that widens any capability. Presence is not the finding.

rag-agent.defect: build_prompt_marked, the hardened twin, is not safe: origin and trust render through !r but d['text'] is interpolated raw, so a ticket body containing a closing document tag escapes the container and injects forged markup inside it.
rag-agent.found_by: an arm under audit, not by a review of the case; two independent adversarial verifiers reached it in bench/runs/2026-08-22-recall-resolution/, one by rendering it
rag-agent.scoring_consequence: claims of the form 'the marking does not prevent injection' are TRUE of this case and must be scored supported. A round that counted them as hits on the safe half would be scoring a real defect as a mistake.
rag-agent.status: left unfixed for now so rounds already scored against this case stay comparable; fixing it changes the key and is its own change

intake-portal.defect: The three inert route guards (P-48, P-49, P-50) are simultaneously an inert control and, in effect, an absent object-level check: the caller header reaches the guard and is never used.
intake-portal.found_by: written into the case deliberately, and recorded here before the first run rather than after one
intake-portal.scoring_consequence: A claim naming WEB-04 or missing object-level authorization on those three handlers is TRUE of this case and must be scored supported, exactly like a claim naming WEB-27. Scoring one of the two readings as a mistake would be scoring a real defect as an error.
intake-portal.status: intended, not a flaw in the case: the two readings are the same line and a corpus that only accepted one of them would be grading vocabulary rather than detection
